text.p: Third-quarter earnings at Seagram Co. Ltd. more than doubled to $27 million, led by higher revenues at its Universal Inc. film and theme park unit, the beverages and entertainment company said on Wednesday.
Seagram reported a net profit for the quarter of $27 million, or 7 cents a share, compared with net income of $13 million, or 4 cents a share, a year earlier.
Revenues rose to $2.8 billion from $2.6 billion.
In the latest nine months, Seagram had a net profit of $354 million, or 96 cents a share, vs. $53 million or 15 cents share a year earlier. Nine-month sales rose to $9.5 billion from $9.2 billion.
Seagram's nine-month results included a $64 million pre-tax gain on the sale of the Putnam Berkley Group Inc. in fiscal 1997, compared with a $290 million restructuring charge in fiscal 1996.
"We are pleased with the company's overall results which were achieved despite difficult market conditions for all our operations," Seagram Chief Executive Edgar Bronfman Jr. said in a statement.
Seagram stock rallied on stock markets in Canada and the United States after the results.
Seagram rose C95 cents to C$53.55 in Toronto, and by 50 cents to $38.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
"The numbers appear to be in line with (Wall) Street estimates -- no major suprises," said David Leibowitz, analyst and managing partner at Burnham Securities in New York.

Seagram said revenues at 80 percent-owned Universal, which makes films, recorded music and operates theme parks, increased 16 percent in the third quarter to $1.6 billion, while its earnings before interest, taxes and depreciation rose 6 percent to $114 million.
The improvement at Universal was driven by its music and theme parks groups, Seagram said.

Revenues for the company's spirits and wine group, which makes alcoholic beverages under high-profile brand names such as Chivas Regal Scotch Whisky and Martell Cognac, were flat at about $1.1 billion, but its pre-tax profits rose 9 percent to $143 million.
Bronfman said the profit improvement in alcoholic beverages was due mainly to benefits from its fiscal 1996 "reengineering."

Seagram's beverage group, which makes fruit juices under the Tropicana and Dole brand name, showed an 8 percent increase in revenues to $534 million, while pre-tax earnings were up 16 percent to $50 million.
Seagram attributed the beverage group's stronger performance to sales of its Tropicana Pure Premium fruit juices.
